question: Can point-in-time cross-sectional differentiation in Taiwan electronics identify when the near-future cross-section will contain more or less differentiation, without assuming that high dispersion itself creates alpha?
reason: This introduces an opportunity-capacity diagnostic distinct from the already-tested static Market State x MOM20 conditioning question.
evidence_summary: International literature commonly treats cross-sectional return dispersion as an active-management opportunity-set variable, but it also warns that dispersion changes performance measurement and can reflect risk rather than skill.

Connolly and Stivers (2006) report that daily cross-sectional return dispersion contains incremental information about future firm- and portfolio-level volatility, supporting a bounded persistence/forecastability test of dispersion itself.
Stivers and Sun (2010) show that recent return dispersion is related differently to subsequent value and momentum premiums; therefore dispersion is not a strategy-neutral guarantee of alpha.

MSCI research decomposes total dispersion into systematic and stock-specific components and notes that high correlation during stress can reduce the stock-specific share even when total dispersion is elevated.

Taiwan-specific 2026 NCCU thesis evidence is directionally contrary to the simple overseas story: high-dispersion months were associated with weaker alpha among more active Taiwan equity funds. The full thesis is embargoed until 2031, so this source is ABSTRACT_ONLY_NOT_FULLY_READ and must not be treated as full-text evidence.

Therefore HENGCE must not preregister 'high dispersion means more alpha'. The defensible first test is narrower: whether a point-in-time differentiation measure predicts subsequent realized cross-sectional differentiation, and how that capacity behaves around frozen state transitions.

gate_constraints: No new BUY/SELL/ranking rule may be created from this gate.
No directional claim that high dispersion implies higher alpha is authorized.
The first experiment must be a diagnostic of opportunity capacity, not strategy optimization.
Any new outcome definition must be preregistered before its forward values are inspected.
Previously inspected 2018-2026 periods remain retrospective/development evidence, not untouched OOS.
